Definition: from G3101; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar:--be disciple, instruct, teach.
BiblicalUsage: To disciple means to make learners, and it is the last command Jesus gave: go and make disciples of all nations. A scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom is like a householder bringing out things new and old, and Paul and Barnabas made many disciples at Derbe before they returned. Joseph of Arimathea, a rich man who had become a disciple, is the one who buried Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that making disciples is the church's real work: not gathering crowds, but teaching people to follow Jesus until His ways become theirs. Joseph shows the other side of it — a disciple is known in the end by what he does with Jesus when it costs him.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Paul; Barnabas; Joseph of Arimathea
RelatedEvents: The Great Commission; The Burial of Jesus
